# Distributed Team Effectiveness
## Reduce the need to communicate before you improve the communication

---

## 0. Three decisions before anything is designed

1. **Decide whether you are willing to re-cut the work.** Conway's law runs in both directions: if a team's critical dependencies span a zero-overlap timezone pair, no protocol, tool or training closes that gap — every dependency costs a calendar day, and a four-step clarification costs a week. Either you are prepared to reallocate ownership so that each hub holds whole, decidable slices of work, or you are funding better meetings about the same broken structure.
2. **Decide that written and asynchronous is the default — and that leadership goes first.** Norms are set by what executives do at 9am in their own timezone, not by what the handbook says. If the leadership team still makes decisions in a room and documents them later (or never), every satellite hub correctly concludes that the real company runs on HQ hours and the async policy is decoration.
3. **Decide what you measure people on.** Any activity-based proxy — hours online, chat responsiveness, green dots, meeting attendance — re-centralises the company on headquarters time and punishes exactly the behaviour you want. You measure decision latency, cycle time and rework. Get this wrong and everything in §5 is theatre.

---

## 1. Unbundle: "communication problems" is five different problems

| | **Structural coupling** | **Decision latency** | **Context loss** | **Interpretation gap** | **Trust deficit** |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| **Symptom** | Constant blocking; "waiting on the other hub" | Escalations stall; nothing moves without HQ | People rediscover known things; the same question answered five times | "That's not what I asked for"; rework; polite agreement then divergence | Us-and-them; assumed incompetence; low-grade resentment |
| **Real driver** | Work split across timezones with interdependent ownership | Authority concentrated in one geography; ambiguous decision rights | Knowledge lives in synchronous meetings half the team can't attend | High- vs low-context norms, fluency asymmetry, power distance, silence read as consent | No shared history; distance amplifies attribution error |
| **Cheapest effective fix** | Reallocate ownership; break the cross-hub dependency | Written decision rights; delegate to hub leads with reversal conditions | Decision records; docs-as-artifact; meetings produce written output or don't count | Explicit team charter of norms; written-first; structured dissent | Periodic co-location; hub exchanges; ambassador pairing |
| **Cost** | Near-zero capex, high political cost | Near-zero — it's a policy change | Low | Low | Moderate (travel) |
| **Tools' role** | None. Tools cannot fix a dependency graph | None | Enablement | Marginal | Marginal |

**The critical connection.** Volume of communication and quality of communication are the same problem. A programme drowning in messages, meetings and clarification threads is usually a programme whose work is badly allocated; the traffic is a symptom of coupling, not of poor writing skills. Reduce the *need* to coordinate and the remaining coordination is high-value, low-frequency, and you can afford to do it properly — synchronously, with video, with the right people.

**Corollary:** do not size your meeting cadence, tooling or "collaboration programme" on today's coordination volume. Size it on post-recut volume, or you will institutionalise the overhead you were trying to remove.

---

## 2. Price the latency — do this arithmetic first

*Illustrative; substitute actuals from Phase 0.*

| | |
|---|---|
| Programme | 8 project teams, ~96 people, 3 hubs |
| Median feature cycle time | 18 working days |
| Of which: waiting on a cross-hub answer or decision | **4.2 days (23%)** |
| Achievable with response tiers + delegated decision rights | ~1.8 days → **~2.4 days recovered per item** |
| Items delivered / year | 240 → **~575 days of throughput ≈ 11% effective capacity** |
| Work items requiring material rework from a misunderstood requirement | 14% → 34 items × 3.5 person-days = **~120 person-days** |
| Median time-to-decision on items requiring HQ sign-off | **6.5 days** (target ≤1.5) |
| Recurring meeting load | 6.5 h/person/week; ~40% status-only → **~1,400 person-days/yr recoverable ≈ €840k** |
| Attrition: satellite hubs vs. HQ | 19% vs 11% → ~5 excess leavers/yr → **~€300k plus 3–6 months' ramp each** |

Two things fall out of this table. First, the schedule cost dwarfs the tooling budget by an order of magnitude — the argument for change is a delivery argument, not a culture argument, and should be presented to the board that way. Second, **the largest single recoverable number is the meeting load**, and it is recoverable in weeks, not quarters. Fund the rest of the programme out of it.

Note the invisible term: the questions people *don't* ask because the round-trip is too expensive. Those become assumptions, and assumptions become the 14% rework line. The visible clarification traffic is the tip.

---

## 3. The overlap budget — timezone geometry is a hard constraint

Compute this before designing anything. It is the single most under-examined number in distributed programmes.

| Pair | Civilised-hours overlap | Status |
|---|---|---|
| Hub A (UTC−8) ↔ Hub B (UTC+1) | ~1–2 h | Thin — ration it |
| Hub B (UTC+1) ↔ Hub C (UTC+5:30) | ~4 h | Workable — this is your main channel |
| Hub A (UTC−8) ↔ Hub C (UTC+5:30) | **~0 h** | **Structurally broken** |
| All three | ~30–45 min/day, painful for two of three | Reserve for the rare event |

**Three design rules follow.**

- **The zero-overlap pair rule.** Never place a tight, iterative dependency across a pair with no overlap. Either eliminate the dependency by reallocating ownership, or route it deliberately through the middle hub as a designed relay with a named steward — never leave it to ad-hoc chasing.
- **Overlap is the scarcest resource in the programme.** Spend it only on ambiguity, conflict and relationship. Any status meeting held in an overlap window is a misallocation of the one asset you cannot buy more of.
- **The timezone tax is rotated, not assigned.** If the same hub always takes the 22:00 call, you have quietly built a two-tier company, and your attrition table will tell you so within a year.

---

## 4. The intervention ladder — climb it in order

| Tier | Content | Cost | Time to effect | Reversibility |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| **0 — Structural** | Re-cut work so each hub owns whole decidable slices; break cross-hub dependencies; publish decision rights; delegate to hub leads with named reversal conditions | Near-zero capex, high political cost | 1–3 months | Low (do it once, do it right) |
| **1 — Operating system** | Async-first defaults; response-time tiers; decision records; handoff protocol; meeting hygiene; single source of truth | Low | 1–4 months | Total |
| **2 — Fluency & inclusion** | Team charter of explicit norms; structured dissent; language practices; participation equity; rotated meeting pain; conflict protocol | Low | 2–6 months | Total |
| **3 — Relational** | Co-location cadence; hub exchanges; ambassador pairing; rotated programme leadership; deliberate onboarding-into-network | Moderate (travel) | 4–12 months | High |

**Design rules.** Tiers 0 and 1 are hygiene, not a phase — everything above them degrades without them. Never solve a structural problem with a meeting; the meeting will recur forever and the structure will not change. And never buy a collaboration tool before Phase 0 is complete: tools encode norms, and a tool bought to fix an undiagnosed problem hard-codes the dysfunction.

---

## 5. The operating system — concrete protocols

### 5.1 Mode selection

Most "communication problems" are mode-selection errors: high-ambiguity work attempted in chat, low-ambiguity status pushed into meetings.

| | **Low emotional stakes** | **High emotional stakes** |
|---|---|---|
| **Low ambiguity** | Async written. Status, FYI, confirmations. Never a meeting. | 1:1 synchronous video. Never a public channel. |
| **High ambiguity** | Async doc + timed comment round → short sync only on the unresolved delta | Facilitated synchronous, video on, small group, neutral chair |

**The three round-trip rule.** If an async thread passes three exchanges without converging, someone books a call. Threads do not die of exhaustion; they die of ambiguity, and the ambiguity survives into the code.

### 5.2 Response-time tiers

Ambiguity about *when* an answer is due generates more latency than any other single factor.

| Tag | Expected response | Backup |
|---|---|---|
| **FYI** | None required | — |
| **Non-blocking** | Next working day of the *recipient* | — |
| **Blocking** | Within 4 working hours of recipient's day |
